CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra|wenyan-lite|wenyan-full|wenyan-ultra|off`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) — tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either — own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Never drop not/never/no/only/except — flip meaning worse than any token saved. Numbers, units exact.

Tool calls: fire direct. No preamble, plan, or progress note before or between calls. After result: next call direct or final answer — never announce next call. Text before call only to clarify, warn security/irreversible, or resolve ambiguity.

Preserve user's dominant language exactly — reply in the language user writes, never switch regardless of example text or multilingual context elsewhere. Compress the style, not the language. Every emitted line in that language — openings, pre-tool status lines, all — not just final reply. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

'Drop articles' = article languages only. Where small markers carry case/role (particles, postpositions), keep them — grammar, not filler; compress politeness/filler instead.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

Classical chars = wenyan modes only. Never swap a word to a classical char to shrink at non-wenyan levels.

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example shows FORMAT only — write warning in session language, not example's.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Persisted outside chat: write normal prose — code, comments, commits, docs, issue/PR/MR text, memory files, third-party messages (/caveman-compress exempt). "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

- caveman: Ultra-compressed communication mode. Cuts token usage ~75% by dropping filler, articles, and pleasantries while keeping full technical accuracy. Use when user says "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "use caveman", "less tokens", "be brief", or invokes /caveman.
- diagnose: Disciplined diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Reproduce → minimise → hypothesise → instrument → fix → regression-test. Use when user says "diagnose this" / "debug this", reports a bug, says something is broken/throwing/failing, or describes a performance regression.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- github-triage: Triage GitHub issues through a label-based state machine. Use when user wants to create an issue, triage issues, review incoming bugs or feature requests, prepare issues for an AFK agent, or manage issue workflow.
- grill-me: Interview the user relentlessly about a plan or design until reaching shared understanding, resolving each branch of the decision tree. Use when user wants to stress-test a plan, get grilled on their design, or mentions "grill me".
- humanizer: Remove signs of AI-generated writing from text. Use when editing or reviewing
text to make it sound more natural and human-written. Based on Wikipedia's
comprehensive "Signs of AI writing" guide. Detects and fixes patterns including:
inflated symbolism, promotional language, superficial -ing analyses, vague
attributions, em dash overuse, rule of three, AI vocabulary words, negative
parallelisms, and excessive conjunctive phrases.
- review-pr-feedback: Walk every unresolved review thread on the current branch's PR — fix what is fixable, ask the user about anything ambiguous, then reply on each thread and mark it resolved. Use when the user says "review PR feedback", "go thru the PR comments", "address review comments", or similar.
- ship: Commit, push, and update the PR description or add a comment based on new changes. Use when the user says "ship it", "commit push and update pr", or similar.

- to-issues: Break a plan, spec, or PRD into independently-grabbable GitHub issues using tracer-bullet vertical slices. Use when user wants to convert a plan into issues, create implementation tickets, or break down work into issues.
- to-prd: Turn the current conversation context into a PRD and submit it as a GitHub issue. Use when user wants to create a PRD from the current context.

## Release Channels

Entire currently ships two release channels:

- `stable`: recommended for most users. Stable releases change less often and are the default for Homebrew, Scoop, and `install.sh`.
- `nightly`: prerelease builds for users who want the latest changes earlier. Nightlies are published more frequently and may include newer, less-proven changes than stable.

How to use each channel:

- Homebrew (one-time setup): `brew tap entireio/tap && brew trust entireio/tap`
- Homebrew stable: `brew install --cask entire`
- Homebrew nightly: `brew install --cask entire@nightly`
- `install.sh` stable: `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`
- `install.sh` nightly: `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly`
- Scoop: currently supports `stable` only via `scoop install entire/cli`

content.text:
Key fact: scoop is **pull-based**. Releasing a v9 `entire/cli` pushes nothing to the user's machine. The new `entire/entire` manifest only reaches their local bucket clone when *they* refresh it. So "release v9 cli → forces download of latest bucket" is false — nothing downloads until a refresh runs on their side.

So plain `scoop uninstall entire/cli && scoop install entire/entire` (no refresh) lands v9 only if their local bucket clone *already* has the current `entire` manifest. Can't guarantee that for a v8 user whose clone is old. The refresh is unavoidable — it's the step that brings the new manifest local.

What releasing a v9 `entire/cli` *does* buy you (independent value):
- Users who never migrate still get updates via the normal `scoop update entire/cli` path — not stranded on v8.
- IF `scoop update <app>` git-pulls the bucket first (it does in modern scoop), then a user upgrading normally to v9-cli gets the `entire` manifest locally as a side effect — so a *later* switch to `entire/entire` needs no explicit refresh.

But that's two moments. In the single migration command, one refresh is still required.

Net: publishing v9-cli is a good idea for continuity, but it doesn't remove the bucket-refresh from the migration command. My current `bucket rm && bucket add` is the minimal, bucket-scoped refresh — no full `scoop update`.

Want me to leave the command as-is, or are you also deciding to keep publishing `entire/cli` (that's a `.goreleaser.yaml` question, separate from this CLI code)?

input.prompt: Does scoop-install.ps1 call is_scoop_outdated? When scoop is outdated, does it automatically run an update/bucket refresh, or does it only print a warning telling the user to run 'scoop update'? Quote the relevant lines around is_scoop_outdated.

content.text:
Confirmed in source. Modern `scoop-install.ps1`:

```powershell
if (is_scoop_outdated) {
    if ($opt.u -or $opt.'no-update-scoop') { warn "Scoop is out of date." }
    else { & "$PSScriptRoot\scoop-update.ps1" }
}
```

So `scoop install entire/entire` auto-runs a bucket refresh when the last update was >3h ago (`is_scoop_outdated`). A migrating v8 user's bucket is effectively always >3h stale (v9 shipped long before), so the `entire` manifest lands automatically before install. You're right — we don't need the explicit refresh.

Simplify to just:

```
scoop uninstall entire/cli && scoop install entire/entire
```

Caveats (small):
- If the user ran a scoop command <3h ago **and** v9 landed inside that window → no refresh, manifest missing → `install` fails cleanly with an error, they rerun later. Rare edge, recoverable.
- When the auto-refresh does fire it's a full `scoop update` (scoop core + all buckets) — the thing you didn't want to force earlier — but now it's scoop-native and conditional, not us forcing it.

# Ship Changes

Commit current changes, push to remote, and update the PR.

## Step 1: Analyze changes

1. Run `git diff --stat` and `git diff` to understand what changed
2. Run `git status` to see untracked files
3. Run `git log --oneline -3` to match the repo's commit message style

## Step 2: Commit

1. Stage only the relevant changed/untracked files by name (never `git add -A` or `git add .`)
2. Write a concise commit message that focuses on the "why" not the "what"
   - If `` is provided, use it as the commit message
   - Otherwise, draft one from the diff
3. Commit. If hooks fail, diagnose and fix — do NOT use `--no-verify`

## Step 3: Push

1. Check if the branch tracks a remote: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}`
2. If not tracking, push with `-u origin <branch>`
3. If tracking, just `git push`
4. If push is rejected (remote has new commits), pull with rebase first then push

## Step 4: Update PR

1. Find the open PR for the current branch: `gh pr view --json number,body,title`
2. If no PR exists, skip this step and inform the user
3. Compare the current PR body against the new changes:
   - If the changes are within the existing PR scope, update the description to reflect the current state
   - If the changes are additive or a follow-up, add a PR comment summarizing what was just pushed instead
4. When updating the PR body, preserve the overall structure but refresh the summary bullets and test plan
5. When adding a comment, keep it concise — bullet points of what changed and why
6. **Before making any PR update (description edit or comment), show the user the exact text you plan to post and ask for their approval. Do NOT post until they confirm.**

## Rules

- Never commit files that look like secrets (.env, credentials, tokens)
- Never force push

{"body":"## Problem

#1735 renamed the Scoop package from `cli` to `entire`. Scoop resolves updates by manifest name, so existing Windows installs registered as app `cli` were orphaned when `cli.json` disappeared from the bucket: `scoop update` finds nothing and they silently stop receiving updates. The only way out for those users today is a manual uninstall + reinstall.

## Fix

Keep publishing `cli.json` as a **transition manifest** alongside the canonical `entire.json`:

- `depends: [entire]` — the next `scoop update cli` automatically installs the canonical `entire` package, no forced reinstall.
- `post_install` prints a migration nudge:
  `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire`
  (the `reset` recovers the shared `entire.exe` shim, which `scoop uninstall cli` can take with it — both apps ship the same shims).
- `skip_upload: auto` matching the existing entry, so prereleases don't push manifests.

GoReleaser bumps both manifests every release, so migration fires naturally on users' next update — including users who already stalled: they resume on their next `scoop update` once the next release republishes `cli.json`.

## Sunset

The transition entry should be dropped a few releases after migration has largely completed (noted in the config comment).

## Validation

- `goreleaser check` passes; `mise run fmt` / `mise run lint` clean.
- Migration flow replayed end-to-end on a Windows VM with a local clone of the bucket:
  - resurrected the pre-rename `cli.json` from bucket history and installed it (simulated existing user),
  - committed the new `entire.json` + transition `cli.json`,
  - `scoop update cli` pulled in `entire` via `depends` and printed the migration message,
  - `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire` leaves a working `entire`.

## Notes / residual risk

- Legacy users who stay on the `cli` app keep the old `apps\cli` install path that fed #1424 — the post_install nudge is the only lever to move them; verify the #1424 fix is path-independent before removing the nudge.
- Old app can't be force-removed from users' machines; the nudge is best-effort by design.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> **Low Risk**
> Release packaging only in `.goreleaser.yaml`; no application or auth logic changes, with behavior limited to Scoop bucket manifests on update.

## Problem

#1735 renamed the Scoop package from `cli` to `entire`. Scoop resolves updates by manifest name, so existing Windows installs registered as app `cli` were orphaned when `cli.json` disappeared from the bucket: `scoop update` finds nothing and they silently stop receiving updates. The only way out for those users today is a manual uninstall + reinstall.

The CLI's own update prompt had the same blind spot: `entire`'s version-check emitted `scoop update entire/cli` for Scoop installs, which can never cross the rename to `entire/entire`.

## Fix

**Bucket side** — keep publishing `cli.json` as a **transition manifest** alongside the canonical `entire.json`:

- `depends: [entire]` — the next `scoop update cli` automatically installs the canonical `entire` package, no forced reinstall.
- `post_install` prints a migration nudge:
  `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire`
  (the `reset` recovers the shared `entire.exe` shim, which `scoop uninstall cli` can take with it — both apps ship the same shims).
- `skip_upload: auto` matching the existing entry, so prereleases don't push manifests.

GoReleaser bumps both manifests every release, so migration fires naturally on users' next update — including users who already stalled: they resume on their next `scoop update` once the next release republishes `cli.json`.

**CLI side** — fix the version-check upgrade command so a pre-rename Scoop install is steered across the rename:

- When the running binary is **pre-v0.9** (installed as the `cli` package) and installed via **Scoop**, `updateCommand` returns `scoop uninstall entire/cli && scoop install entire/entire` instead of `scoop update entire/cli`. v0.9+ installs update via `scoop update entire/entire`.
- No explicit bucket refresh is needed: `scoop install` auto-runs `scoop-update.ps1` when the bucket is >3h stale (`is_scoop_outdated` in `lib/core.ps1`; auto-update call in `libexec/scoop-install.ps1`), so the new `entire` manifest lands before install.
- Other install managers (brew, mise, curl) are unchanged.
- README Windows section documents the same manual steps.

## Sunset

The transition entry should be dropped a few releases after migration has largely completed (noted in the config comment).

## Validation

- `goreleaser check` passes; `mise run fmt` / `mise run lint` clean.
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/` passes, incl. cases asserting the pre-v0.9 Scoop path emits the uninstall+install command and v0.9+ updates `entire/entire`.
- Migration flow replayed end-to-end on a Windows VM with a local clone of the bucket:
  - resurrected the pre-rename `cli.json` from bucket history and installed it (simulated existing user),
  - committed the new `entire.json` + transition `cli.json`,
  - `scoop update cli` pulled in `entire` via `depends` and printed the migration message,
  - `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire` leaves a working `entire`.

## Notes / residual risk

- Legacy users who stay on the `cli` app keep the old `apps\cli` install path that fed #1424 — the post_install nudge is the only lever to move them; verify the #1424 fix is path-independent before removing the nudge.
- Old app can't be force-removed from users' machines; the nudge is best-effort by design.
- The CLI pre-v0.9 command relies on Scoop's >3h staleness auto-refresh; if a user ran a scoop command <3h before migrating and the new release landed inside that window, `scoop install entire/entire` fails cleanly (missing manifest) and succeeds on retry.

Careful — the auto-run path executes via `cmd /C` (autoupdate.go), where `&&` is valid; your error is from pasting into PowerShell by hand. But swapping to `;` while keeping `cmd /C` **breaks the real path** — `;` isn't a command separator in cmd.exe, it'd be passed as a literal arg.

Scoop is a PowerShell tool, so the right fix is: run the Windows installer via **PowerShell** and use `;`. Then the string works both when auto-run and when a user copy-pastes it. Bonus: `;` continues to the install even if the uninstall hiccups (e.g. already gone) — better for migration than `&&` aborting.

## Problem

#1735 renamed the Scoop package from `cli` to `entire`. Scoop resolves updates by manifest name, so existing Windows installs registered as app `cli` were orphaned when `cli.json` disappeared from the bucket: `scoop update` finds nothing and they silently stop receiving updates. The only way out for those users today is a manual uninstall + reinstall.

The CLI's own update prompt had the same blind spot: `entire`'s version-check emitted `scoop update entire/cli` for Scoop installs, which can never cross the rename to `entire/entire`.

## Fix

**Bucket side** — keep publishing `cli.json` as a **transition manifest** alongside the canonical `entire.json`:

- `depends: [entire]` — the next `scoop update cli` automatically installs the canonical `entire` package, no forced reinstall.
- `post_install` prints a migration nudge:
  `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire`
  (the `reset` recovers the shared `entire.exe` shim, which `scoop uninstall cli` can take with it — both apps ship the same shims).
- `skip_upload: auto` matching the existing entry, so prereleases don't push manifests.

GoReleaser bumps both manifests every release, so migration fires naturally on users' next update — including users who already stalled: they resume on their next `scoop update` once the next release republishes `cli.json`.

**CLI side** — fix the version-check upgrade command so a pre-rename Scoop install is steered across the rename:

- When the running binary is **pre-v0.9** (installed as the `cli` package) and installed via **Scoop**, `updateCommand` returns `scoop uninstall entire/cli && scoop install entire/entire` instead of `scoop update entire/cli`. v0.9+ installs update via `scoop update entire/entire`.
- No explicit bucket refresh is needed: `scoop install` auto-runs `scoop-update.ps1` when the bucket is >3h stale (`is_scoop_outdated` in `lib/core.ps1`; auto-update call in `libexec/scoop-install.ps1`), so the new `entire` manifest lands before install.
- Other install managers (brew, mise, curl) are unchanged.
- README Windows section documents the same manual steps.

## Sunset

The transition entry should be dropped a few releases after migration has largely completed (noted in the config comment).

## Validation

- `goreleaser check` passes; `mise run fmt` / `mise run lint` clean.
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/` passes, incl. cases asserting the pre-v0.9 Scoop path emits the uninstall+install command and v0.9+ updates `entire/entire`.
- Migration flow replayed end-to-end on a Windows VM with a local clone of the bucket:
  - resurrected the pre-rename `cli.json` from bucket history and installed it (simulated existing user),
  - committed the new `entire.json` + transition `cli.json`,
  - `scoop update cli` pulled in `entire` via `depends` and printed the migration message,
  - `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire` leaves a working `entire`.

## Notes / residual risk

- Legacy users who stay on the `cli` app keep the old `apps\cli` install path that fed #1424 — the post_install nudge is the only lever to move them; verify the #1424 fix is path-independent before removing the nudge.
- Old app can't be force-removed from users' machines; the nudge is best-effort by design.
- The CLI pre-v0.9 command relies on Scoop's >3h staleness auto-refresh; if a user ran a scoop command <3h before migrating and the new release landed inside that window, `scoop install entire/entire` fails cleanly (missing manifest) and succeeds on retry.

content.text:
Verified. The canonical `entire` manifest already lives on `main` — this PR's **only** goreleaser change is the transition `cli` manifest (commit `33aa84520`, the PR's base).

Key finding: the CLI fix's command `scoop install entire/entire` depends on the **canonical `entire` manifest** (already live), **not** on the transition `cli` manifest. So the CLI fix works without it.

But they're **not fully redundant** — they cover different trigger channels for a pre-rename `cli`-app install:

| | Transition `cli` manifest | CLI version-check fix |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | user runs `scoop update` (scoop's own updater) | user runs `entire` (any command) |
| Needs user to run `entire`? | **No** — passive | **Yes** |
| If bucket already dropped `cli.json` | revives the `scoop update` path | only recovery for those users |

So:
- **Strictly needed for the CLI fix to work?** No.
- **What's lost if you drop it?** The *passive* migration path — a user who updates via plain `scoop update` and never watches `entire`'s output stops getting scoop-native updates until they run `entire` and follow the prompt. Also the `post_install` nudge disappears.

My recommendation: **keep it** — it's zero runtime cost and the only channel that reaches passive `scoop update` users. The two together are belt-and-suspenders.

But if you'd rather make the CLI prompt the sole migration path and slim the PR to just the code + README, I can revert `33aa84520`. Want me to drop it, or keep it?

content.text:
Good catch — that's the core flaw. `if ($?)` and forcing PowerShell are shell-specific, and the command string does double duty: auto-run **and** printed for the user to paste into whatever shell they're in (cmd, PowerShell, pwsh, git-bash). A conditional can't be shell-agnostic.

Resolution: make the migration command a **single, shell-agnostic** `scoop install entire/entire`. That:
- Is safe by construction — it never removes the working CLI, so the reviewer's P1 (don't leave the user without an executable) is fully satisfied without any conditional.
- Migrates the user: `scoop install` auto-refreshes the bucket and the most-recent install owns the shared `entire.exe` shim (per the manifest's own note), so `entire` now runs the new app.
- Cleanup of the old `cli` app is left to the transition manifest's `post_install` nudge (fires on `scoop update`) — not the auto-command's job.

And revert the PowerShell exec back to the original.

## Entire trail

[#1023 — Fix Scoop cli->entire upgrade path](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1023)

## Problem

#1735 renamed the Scoop package from `cli` to `entire`. Scoop resolves updates by manifest name, so existing Windows installs registered as app `cli` were orphaned when `cli.json` disappeared from the bucket: `scoop update` finds nothing and they silently stop receiving updates. The only way out for those users today is a manual uninstall + reinstall.

The CLI's own update prompt had the same blind spot: `entire`'s version-check emitted `scoop update entire/cli` for Scoop installs, which can never cross the rename to `entire/entire`.

## Fix

**Bucket side** — keep publishing `cli.json` as a **transition manifest** alongside the canonical `entire.json`:

- `depends: [entire]` — the next `scoop update cli` automatically installs the canonical `entire` package, no forced reinstall.
- `post_install` prints a migration nudge:
  `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire`
  (the `reset` recovers the shared `entire.exe` shim, which `scoop uninstall cli` can take with it — both apps ship the same shims).
- `skip_upload: auto` matching the existing entry, so prereleases don't push manifests.

GoReleaser bumps both manifests every release, so migration fires naturally on users' next update — including users who already stalled: they resume on their next `scoop update` once the next release republishes `cli.json`.

**CLI side** — fix the version-check upgrade command so a pre-rename Scoop install is steered across the rename:

- When the running binary is **pre-v0.9** (installed as the `cli` package) and installed via **Scoop**, `updateCommand` returns `scoop uninstall entire/cli && scoop install entire/entire` instead of `scoop update entire/cli`. v0.9+ installs update via `scoop update entire/entire`.
- No explicit bucket refresh is needed: `scoop install` auto-runs `scoop-update.ps1` when the bucket is >3h stale (`is_scoop_outdated` in `lib/core.ps1`; auto-update call in `libexec/scoop-install.ps1`), so the new `entire` manifest lands before install.
- Other install managers (brew, mise, curl) are unchanged.
- README Windows section documents the same manual steps.

## Example (pre-rename Scoop install on Windows)

```text
PS C:\Users\Victor\cli> entire version
Entire CLI 0.8.0
Go version: go1.26.5
OS/Arch: windows/arm64

Update available! 0.8.0 -> 0.9.0
Release notes: https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/tag/v0.9.0
To update, run:
  scoop uninstall entire/cli; scoop install entire/entire
```

## Sunset

The transition entry should be dropped a few releases after migration has largely completed (noted in the config comment).

## Validation

- `goreleaser check` passes; `mise run fmt` / `mise run lint` clean.
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/` passes, incl. cases asserting the pre-v0.9 Scoop path emits the uninstall+install command and v0.9+ updates `entire/entire`.
- Migration flow replayed end-to-end on a Windows VM with a local clone of the bucket:
  - resurrected the pre-rename `cli.json` from bucket history and installed it (simulated existing user),
  - committed the new `entire.json` + transition `cli.json`,
  - `scoop update cli` pulled in `entire` via `depends` and printed the migration message,
  - `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire` leaves a working `entire`.

## Notes / residual risk

- Legacy users who stay on the `cli` app keep the old `apps\cli` install path that fed #1424 — the post_install nudge is the only lever to move them; verify the #1424 fix is path-independent before removing the nudge.
- Old app can't be force-removed from users' machines; the nudge is best-effort by design.
- The CLI pre-v0.9 command relies on Scoop's >3h staleness auto-refresh; if a user ran a scoop command <3h before migrating and the new release landed inside that window, `scoop install entire/entire` fails cleanly (missing manifest) and succeeds on retry.

## Entire trail

[#1023 — Fix Scoop cli->entire upgrade path](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1023)

## Problem

#1735 renamed the Scoop package from `cli` to `entire`. Scoop resolves updates by manifest name, so existing Windows installs registered as app `cli` were orphaned when `cli.json` disappeared from the bucket: `scoop update` finds nothing and they silently stop receiving updates. The only way out for those users today is a manual uninstall + reinstall.

The CLI's own update prompt had the same blind spot: `entire`'s version-check emitted `scoop update entire/cli` for Scoop installs, which can never cross the rename to `entire/entire`.

## Fix

**Bucket side** — keep publishing `cli.json` as a **transition manifest** alongside the canonical `entire.json`:

- `depends: [entire]` — the next `scoop update cli` automatically installs the canonical `entire` package, no forced reinstall.
- `post_install` prints a migration nudge:
  `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire`
  (the `reset` recovers the shared `entire.exe` shim, which `scoop uninstall cli` can take with it — both apps ship the same shims).
- `skip_upload: auto` matching the existing entry, so prereleases don't push manifests.

GoReleaser bumps both manifests every release, so migration fires naturally on users' next update — including users who already stalled: they resume on their next `scoop update` once the next release republishes `cli.json`.

**CLI side** — fix the version-check upgrade command so an install still on the old `cli` Scoop app is steered across the rename:

- The gate is the **Scoop app dir the binary runs from** (`…\scoop\apps\cli\…` vs `…\apps\entire\…`), **not the version**. The fix only ships in a binary the user installs by updating their existing `cli` app, so by the time it runs the version is already past the rename — the app-dir name is the durable signal. Binaries on the `cli` app return `scoop install entire/entire`; binaries already on `entire` update in place via `scoop update entire/entire`.
- The migration is a **single, shell-agnostic command** (`scoop install entire/entire`). The update string is both auto-run and printed for the user to paste into any shell (cmd, PowerShell, git-bash, WSL), so it carries no `;`/`&&`/conditional. Installing without removing the old package can never leave the user without a working CLI (addresses the install-before-uninstall review). `scoop install` also auto-refreshes the bucket when >3h stale (`is_scoop_outdated` in `lib/core.ps1`; auto-update in `libexec/scoop-install.ps1`), and the most-recent install owns the shared `entire.exe` shim — so one command migrates the user. Cleanup of the leftover `cli` app stays with the transition manifest's `post_install` nudge.
- Other install managers (brew, mise, curl) are unchanged.
- README Windows section documents the manual migration (install first, then optional cleanup).

## Example (install still on the old `cli` Scoop app, Windows)

```text

Entire CLI 0.8.0
Go version: go1.26.5
OS/Arch: windows/arm64

Update available! 0.8.0 -> 0.9.0
Release notes: https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/tag/v0.9.0
To update, run:
  scoop install entire/entire
```

## Sunset

The transition entry should be dropped a few releases after migration has largely completed (noted in the config comment).

## Validation

- `goreleaser check` passes; `mise run fmt` / `mise run lint` clean.
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/` passes, incl. cases asserting the pre-v0.9 Scoop path emits the uninstall+install command and v0.9+ updates `entire/entire`.
- Migration flow replayed end-to-end on a Windows VM with a local clone of the bucket:
  - resurrected the pre-rename `cli.json` from bucket history and installed it (simulated existing user),
  - committed the new `entire.json` + transition `cli.json`,
  - `scoop update cli` pulled in `entire` via `depends` and printed the migration message,
  - `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire` leaves a working `entire`.

## Notes / residual risk

- Legacy users who stay on the `cli` app keep the old `apps\cli` install path that fed #1424 — the post_install nudge is the only lever to move them; verify the #1424 fix is path-independent before removing the nudge.
- Old app can't be force-removed from users' machines; the nudge is best-effort by design.

attachment.prompt: why is that hard to just use ;?

content.text:
Fair question. The only real blocker is **cmd.exe**. `;` sequences fine in PowerShell and bash — but our auto-run path shells out via `cmd /C` (autoupdate.go), and in cmd.exe `;` is **not** a separator; it gets passed as a literal argument to the first `scoop`. So `cmd /C "scoop install entire/entire; scoop uninstall entire/cli"` breaks.

So `;` "just works" only if we run the auto-exec under PowerShell/bash instead of cmd. Note: the *string* `... ; ... ; ...` isn't PowerShell-specific — `;` is universal across PS and bash; it's cmd.exe specifically that chokes. And the scoop branch only ever fires on a real Windows scoop install (a WSL binary isn't under `scoop\apps\`), so the "user might be in WSL" worry doesn't hit this path.

Two honest options:

**A — just use `;`** (what you're asking): string = `scoop install entire/entire; scoop uninstall entire/cli; scoop reset entire`, and switch the Windows auto-exec to PowerShell. Simple. Two downsides: (1) auto-exec runs under PS not cmd; (2) `;` is unconditional — the uninstall runs **even if the install failed**, which is the exact P1 the reviewer raised (could remove the working CLI after a failed install).

**B — line-split** (what I just built): three plain lines, no separator; runInstaller runs each as its own process and **stops if install fails**. Works under cmd auto-exec *and* any paste shell. Costs a 5-line loop.

B is safer and simpler at the string level; A is simpler at the code level but reintroduces the P1 and forces a PS exec.

Which do you want? I'll finish whichever — I'm mid-way on B but can drop to plain `;` in a minute.

## Entire trail

[#1023 — Fix Scoop cli->entire upgrade path](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1023)

## Problem

#1735 renamed the Scoop package from `cli` to `entire`. Scoop resolves updates by manifest name, so existing Windows installs registered as app `cli` were orphaned when `cli.json` disappeared from the bucket: `scoop update` finds nothing and they silently stop receiving updates. The only way out for those users today is a manual uninstall + reinstall.

The CLI's own update prompt had the same blind spot: `entire`'s version-check emitted `scoop update entire/cli` for Scoop installs, which can never cross the rename to `entire/entire`.

## Fix

**Bucket side** — keep publishing `cli.json` as a **transition manifest** alongside the canonical `entire.json`:

- `depends: [entire]` — the next `scoop update cli` automatically installs the canonical `entire` package, no forced reinstall.
- `post_install` prints a migration nudge:
  `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire`
  (the `reset` recovers the shared `entire.exe` shim, which `scoop uninstall cli` can take with it — both apps ship the same shims).
- `skip_upload: auto` matching the existing entry, so prereleases don't push manifests.

GoReleaser bumps both manifests every release, so migration fires naturally on users' next update — including users who already stalled: they resume on their next `scoop update` once the next release republishes `cli.json`.

**CLI side** — fix the version-check upgrade command so an install still on the old `cli` Scoop app is steered across the rename:

- The gate is the **Scoop app dir the binary runs from** (`…\scoop\apps\cli\…` vs `…\apps\entire\…`), **not the version**. The fix only ships in a binary the user installs by updating their existing `cli` app, so by the time it runs the version is already past the rename — the app-dir name is the durable signal. Binaries on the `cli` app return `scoop install entire/entire`; binaries already on `entire` update in place via `scoop update entire/entire`.
- The migration is a **single, shell-agnostic command** (`scoop install entire/entire`). The update string is both auto-run and printed for the user to paste into any shell (cmd, PowerShell, git-bash, WSL), so it carries no `;`/`&&`/conditional. Installing without removing the old package can never leave the user without a working CLI (addresses the install-before-uninstall review). `scoop install` also auto-refreshes the bucket when >3h stale (`is_scoop_outdated` in `lib/core.ps1`; auto-update in `libexec/scoop-install.ps1`), and the most-recent install owns the shared `entire.exe` shim — so one command migrates the user. Cleanup of the leftover `cli` app stays with the transition manifest's `post_install` nudge.
- Other install managers (brew, mise, curl) are unchanged.
- README Windows section documents the manual migration (install first, then optional cleanup).

## Example (install still on the old `cli` Scoop app, Windows)

```text
PS C:\Users\Victor\cli> entire version
Entire CLI 0.8.0
Go version: go1.26.5
OS/Arch: windows/arm64

Update available! 0.8.0 -> 0.9.0
Release notes: https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/tag/v0.9.0
To update, run:
  scoop install entire/entire
```

## Sunset

The transition entry should be dropped a few releases after migration has largely completed (noted in the config comment).

## Validation

- `goreleaser check` passes; `mise run fmt` / `mise run lint` clean.
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/` passes, incl. cases asserting the `cli`-app path emits `scoop install entire/entire` and the `entire`-app path updates in place.
- Migration flow replayed end-to-end on a Windows VM with a local clone of the bucket:
  - resurrected the pre-rename `cli.json` from bucket history and installed it (simulated existing user),
  - committed the new `entire.json` + transition `cli.json`,
  - `scoop update cli` pulled in `entire` via `depends` and printed the migration message,
  - `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire` leaves a working `entire`.

## Notes / residual risk

- Legacy users who stay on the `cli` app keep the old `apps\cli` install path that fed #1424 — the post_install nudge is the only lever to move them; verify the #1424 fix is path-independent before removing the nudge.
- Old app can't be force-removed from users' machines; the nudge is best-effort by design.
- The CLI migration command relies on Scoop's >3h staleness auto-refresh; if a user ran a scoop command <3h before migrating and the new release landed inside that window, `scoop install entire/entire` fails cleanly (missing manifest, working CLI untouched) and succeeds on retry.

## Entire trail

[#1023 — Fix Scoop cli->entire upgrade path](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1023)

## Problem

#1735 renamed the Scoop package from `cli` to `entire`. Scoop resolves updates by manifest name, so existing Windows installs registered as app `cli` were orphaned when `cli.json` disappeared from the bucket: `scoop update` finds nothing and they silently stop receiving updates. The only way out for those users today is a manual uninstall + reinstall.

The CLI's own update prompt had the same blind spot: `entire`'s version-check emitted `scoop update entire/cli` for Scoop installs, which can never cross the rename to `entire/entire`.

## Fix

**Bucket side** — keep publishing `cli.json` as a **transition manifest** alongside the canonical `entire.json`:

- `depends: [entire]` — the next `scoop update cli` automatically installs the canonical `entire` package, no forced reinstall.
- `post_install` prints a migration nudge:
  `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire`
  (the `reset` recovers the shared `entire.exe` shim, which `scoop uninstall cli` can take with it — both apps ship the same shims).
- `skip_upload: auto` matching the existing entry, so prereleases don't push manifests.

GoReleaser bumps both manifests every release, so migration fires naturally on users' next update — including users who already stalled: they resume on their next `scoop update` once the next release republishes `cli.json`.

**CLI side** — fix the version-check upgrade command so an install still on the old `cli` Scoop app is steered across the rename:

- The gate is the **Scoop app dir the binary runs from** (`…\scoop\apps\cli\…` vs `…\apps\entire\…`), **not the version**. The fix only ships in a binary the user installs by updating their existing `cli` app, so by the time it runs the version is already past the rename — the app-dir name is the durable signal. Binaries on the `cli` app get the migration below; binaries already on `entire` update in place via `scoop update entire/entire`.
- The migration is **three separate one-command lines** — `scoop install entire/entire`, `scoop uninstall entire/cli`, `scoop reset entire` — **not a shell one-liner**. `realRunInstaller` runs each line as its own process and stops on the first failure, so the uninstall only runs once the install has succeeded (addresses the install-before-uninstall review: a stale bucket or transient failure never leaves the user without a working CLI). Because there is no `;`/`&&`/conditional, the same string is safe to auto-run *and* to paste line-by-line into any shell (cmd, PowerShell, git-bash, WSL). `scoop install` auto-refreshes the bucket when >3h stale (`is_scoop_outdated` in `lib/core.ps1`; auto-update in `libexec/scoop-install.ps1`), and `scoop reset` re-links the shared `entire.exe` shim that uninstalling `cli` can take with it.
- Other install managers (brew, mise, curl) are unchanged.
- README Windows section documents the same manual migration.

## Example (install still on the old `cli` Scoop app, Windows)

```text
PS C:\Users\Victor\cli> entire version
Entire CLI 0.8.0
Go version: go1.26.5
OS/Arch: windows/arm64

Update available! 0.8.0 -> 0.9.0
Release notes: https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/tag/v0.9.0
To update, run:
  scoop install entire/entire
  scoop uninstall entire/cli
  scoop reset entire
```

## Sunset

The transition entry should be dropped a few releases after migration has largely completed (noted in the config comment).

## Validation

- `goreleaser check` passes; `mise run fmt` / `mise run lint` clean.
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/` passes, incl. cases asserting the `cli`-app path emits `scoop install entire/entire` and the `entire`-app path updates in place.
- Migration flow replayed end-to-end on a Windows VM with a local clone of the bucket:
  - resurrected the pre-rename `cli.json` from bucket history and installed it (simulated existing user),
  - committed the new `entire.json` + transition `cli.json`,
  - `scoop update cli` pulled in `entire` via `depends` and printed the migration message,
  - `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire` leaves a working `entire`.

## Notes / residual risk

- Legacy users who stay on the `cli` app keep the old `apps\cli` install path that fed #1424 — the post_install nudge is the only lever to move them; verify the #1424 fix is path-independent before removing the nudge.
- Old app can't be force-removed from users' machines; the nudge is best-effort by design.
- The CLI migration command relies on Scoop's >3h staleness auto-refresh; if a user ran a scoop command <3h before migrating and the new release landed inside that window, `scoop install entire/entire` fails cleanly (missing manifest, working CLI untouched) and succeeds on retry.

aiTitle: Simplify Windows v8 upgrade with Scoop commands

content.text:
Found it — the culprit is Windows-specific. `CanPromptInteractively()` (interactive.go:55) probes `os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", …)`, which **doesn't exist on Windows** → returns `false`. So on Windows, unless overridden, the version check always falls to the printed-hint branch and never shows the interactive "Update now" prompt.

The override is the first check (line 37): `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1` forces interactive on.

Recipe (PowerShell):

```powershell
$env:ENTIRE_TEST_TTY = "1"                                          # force interactive prompt
Remove-Item "$env:USERPROFILE\.config\entire\version_check.json" -ErrorAction Ignore  # clear 24h cache + any "skip until next version"
Remove-Item Env:ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE -ErrorAction Ignore          # ensure kill switch off
Remove-Item Env:CI -ErrorAction Ignore                             # ensure CI gate off

entire status        # post-run version check now shows the huh prompt
```

Requirements that must all hold (else it silently falls back to the hint):
- **`ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1`** — bypasses the `/dev/tty` probe that always fails on Windows.
- **Real console** — run directly in the PowerShell/terminal window (not piped/redirected), so stderr is a terminal (`isTerminalOut`).
- **Outdated** — binary version < latest stable (v0.9.0); a `0.8.x` build qualifies.
- **Fresh cache** — the delete above; otherwise the 24h window or a prior "skip until next version" suppresses it.
- Kill switch `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` and `CI` unset.

Then pick **"Update now"** — it runs the three scoop lines sequentially via `realRunInstaller`.

Note: `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY` is a test seam; fine for manual testing, just don't leave it set in your shell profile.

content: CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (full) — session ruleset applies.

content.text:
That output is the real, load-bearing finding: **you can't self-replace a running Windows binary.** The live `entire` process (Id 4600) holds a lock on its own `shims\entire.exe`, so:

- `scoop install entire/entire` installed the new app dir but **couldn't overwrite the shim** → `entire` still points at the old `cli` app.
- `scoop uninstall entire/cli` **failed** — "instances of cli still running" (that's the very process running the update).
- `scoop reset entire` **failed** the shim relink for the same lock.

So auto-running the migration *from inside* `entire` can't work on Windows. Two important consequences:

**1. In production this path isn't even reached.** On Windows `CanPromptInteractively()` returns false (no `/dev/tty`), so normal Windows users get the **printed list**, never the auto-run. You only hit the broken auto-run because you forced `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1`. Drop that var and you get the intended behavior:

```powershell
Remove-Item Env:ENTIRE_TEST_TTY
entire version
# prints "To update, run:" + the 3 lines — copy them, run in a shell where entire isn't running
```

Run manually (no `entire` process alive), all three succeed.

**2. Recover your current half-migrated state** (new app installed, shim still on cli, cli not removed). `entire` isn't running now, so:

```powershell
scoop uninstall entire/cli
scoop reset entire
entire version   # should now report 0.9.0 from the entire app
```

Now the design question: relying on the `/dev/tty` probe *accidentally* failing on Windows is what keeps us on the safe print-only path. That's incidental, not deliberate — a future Windows TTY-detection improvement would re-enable the prompt and re-break self-update. Want me to make it **explicit**: on Windows, always print the migration commands and never auto-run (so it's correct by design, not by accident)? I'd recommend yes.

message.content: is there any way that /dev/tty would exist on windows env? like running in wsl ?

content: CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (full) — session ruleset applies.

content.text:
Short answer: not for the binary that hits this path.

Two distinct worlds:

- **WSL** = a real Linux environment, so `/dev/tty` exists there — but the `entire` you run in WSL is a **Linux build (`GOOS=linux`)**, and it lives on the Linux filesystem, **not** under `…\scoop\apps\`. So it takes the non-Windows branch entirely and the scoop migration never fires. `/dev/tty` existing there is irrelevant to the scoop case.
- **Native Windows `entire.exe`** (`GOOS=windows`, the only build that can be a scoop install): `os.OpenFile("/dev/tty")` uses Win32 file APIs, and `/dev/tty` isn't a valid Win32 path — it doesn't exist. Even under Git Bash/MSYS2 (which fake a `/dev/tty` for their *own* runtime), a native Go `.exe` doesn't link that runtime, so the probe still fails. Calling `entire.exe` from a WSL shell via interop is still a Windows binary → same result.

So the scoop-migration + Windows-self-lock combo only exists for `GOOS=windows` builds, where `/dev/tty` never resolves → always print-only in practice.

But that's the *accident* protecting us, not intent. The self-lock is real and permanent (a running Windows exe can't replace its own shim), so the robust move is an **explicit `GOOS=windows` guard**: never auto-run the installer on Windows, always print the commands for the user to run when `entire` isn't live. That way it can't break if TTY detection ever changes. Want me to add that guard?

The split only earns its keep if a multi-line command is ever *auto-run*, and the guard guarantees that never happens. YAGNI → remove it.

## Entire trail

[#1023 — Fix Scoop cli->entire upgrade path](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1023)

## Problem

#1735 renamed the Scoop package from `cli` to `entire`. Scoop resolves updates by manifest name, so existing Windows installs registered as app `cli` were orphaned when `cli.json` disappeared from the bucket: `scoop update` finds nothing and they silently stop receiving updates. The only way out for those users today is a manual uninstall + reinstall.

The CLI's own update prompt had the same blind spot: `entire`'s version-check emitted `scoop update entire/cli` for Scoop installs, which can never cross the rename to `entire/entire`.

## Fix

**Bucket side** — keep publishing `cli.json` as a **transition manifest** alongside the canonical `entire.json`:

- `depends: [entire]` — the next `scoop update cli` automatically installs the canonical `entire` package, no forced reinstall.
- `post_install` prints a migration nudge:
  `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire`
  (the `reset` recovers the shared `entire.exe` shim, which `scoop uninstall cli` can take with it — both apps ship the same shims).
- `skip_upload: auto` matching the existing entry, so prereleases don't push manifests.

GoReleaser bumps both manifests every release, so migration fires naturally on users' next update — including users who already stalled: they resume on their next `scoop update` once the next release republishes `cli.json`.

**CLI side** — fix the version-check upgrade command so an install still on the old `cli` Scoop app is steered across the rename:

- The gate is the **Scoop app dir the binary runs from** (`…\scoop\apps\cli\…` vs `…\apps\entire\…`), **not the version**. The fix only ships in a binary the user installs by updating their existing `cli` app, so by the time it runs the version is already past the rename — the app-dir name is the durable signal. Binaries on the `cli` app get the migration below; binaries already on `entire` update in place via `scoop update entire/entire`.
- The migration is **three separate one-command lines** — `scoop install entire/entire`, `scoop uninstall entire/cli`, `scoop reset entire` — **not a shell one-liner**. `realRunInstaller` runs each line as its own process and stops on the first failure, so the uninstall only runs once the install has succeeded (addresses the install-before-uninstall review: a stale bucket or transient failure never leaves the user without a working CLI). Because there is no `;`/`&&`/conditional, the same string is safe to auto-run *and* to paste line-by-line into any shell (cmd, PowerShell, git-bash, WSL). `scoop install` auto-refreshes the bucket when >3h stale (`is_scoop_outdated` in `lib/core.ps1`; auto-update in `libexec/scoop-install.ps1`), and `scoop reset` re-links the shared `entire.exe` shim that uninstalling `cli` can take with it.
- Other install managers (brew, mise, curl) are unchanged.
- README Windows section documents the same manual migration.

Go version: go1.26.5
OS/Arch: windows/arm64

Release notes: https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/tag/v0.9.0

  scoop uninstall entire/cli
  scoop reset entire
```

The transition entry should be dropped a few releases after migration has largely completed (noted in the config comment).

  - resurrected the pre-rename `cli.json` from bucket history and installed it (simulated existing user),

## Entire trail

[#1023 — Fix Scoop cli->entire upgrade path](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1023)

## Problem

#1735 renamed the Scoop package from `cli` to `entire`. Scoop resolves updates by manifest name, so existing Windows installs registered as app `cli` were orphaned when `cli.json` disappeared from the bucket: `scoop update` finds nothing and they silently stop receiving updates. The only way out for those users today is a manual uninstall + reinstall.

The CLI's own update prompt had the same blind spot: `entire`'s version-check emitted `scoop update entire/cli` for Scoop installs, which can never cross the rename to `entire/entire`.

## Fix

**Bucket side** — keep publishing `cli.json` as a **transition manifest** alongside the canonical `entire.json`:

- `depends: [entire]` — the next `scoop update cli` automatically installs the canonical `entire` package, no forced reinstall.
- `post_install` prints a migration nudge:
  `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire`
  (the `reset` recovers the shared `entire.exe` shim, which `scoop uninstall cli` can take with it — both apps ship the same shims).
- `skip_upload: auto` matching the existing entry, so prereleases don't push manifests.

GoReleaser bumps both manifests every release, so migration fires naturally on users' next update — including users who already stalled: they resume on their next `scoop update` once the next release republishes `cli.json`.

**CLI side** — fix the version-check upgrade command so an install still on the old `cli` Scoop app is steered across the rename:

- The gate is the **Scoop app dir the binary runs from** (`…\scoop\apps\cli\…` vs `…\apps\entire\…`), **not the version**. The fix only ships in a binary the user installs by updating their existing `cli` app, so by the time it runs the version is already past the rename — the app-dir name is the durable signal. Binaries on the `cli` app get the migration below; binaries already on `entire` update in place via `scoop update entire/entire`.
- The migration is **three separate one-command lines** — `scoop install entire/entire`, `scoop uninstall entire/cli`, `scoop reset entire` — install first (so a stale bucket or transient failure never removes the working CLI before its replacement is in place), then remove the old package, then `scoop reset` to re-link the shared `entire.exe` shim that uninstalling `cli` can take with it. `scoop install` auto-refreshes the bucket when >3h stale (`is_scoop_outdated` in `lib/core.ps1`; auto-update in `libexec/scoop-install.ps1`).
- **Windows is print-only — the CLI never auto-runs the update.** A running `entire.exe` holds its own shim open, so Scoop can't relink or uninstall it mid-run (install leaves the shim on the old package; uninstall fails with "still running"). So the commands are printed for the user to run once `entire` has exited — no shell operators, so each line pastes into any shell (cmd, PowerShell, git-bash). Because Windows never auto-runs, the runner stays a simple single-command exec.
- Other install managers (brew, mise, curl) are unchanged.
- README Windows section documents the same manual migration.

Entire CLI 0.8.0
Go version: go1.26.5
OS/Arch: windows/arm64

Update available! 0.8.0 -> 0.9.0
Release notes: https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/tag/v0.9.0
To update, run:
  scoop install entire/entire
  scoop uninstall entire/cli
  scoop reset entire
```

The transition entry should be dropped a few releases after migration has largely completed (noted in the config comment).

- `goreleaser check` passes; `mise run fmt` / `mise run lint` clean.

  - committed the new `entire.json` + transition `cli.json`,

  - `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire` leaves a working `entire`.

- Old app can't be force-removed from users' machines; the nudge is best-effort by design.

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://goreleaser.com/static/schema-pro.json
version: 2
pro: true

before:
  hooks:
    - go mod tidy
    - mise run completions

builds:
  - id: entire
    main: ./cmd/entire
    binary: entire
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    goos:
      - darwin
      - linux
      - windows
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    ldflags:
      - -s -w
      - -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo.Version={{.Version}}
      - -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo.Commit={{.ShortCommit}}
      - -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/telemetry.PostHogAPIKey={{.Env.POSTHOG_API_KEY}}
      - -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/telemetry.PostHogEndpoint={{.Env.POSTHOG_ENDPOINT}}
      # Experimental-command visibility: hide in stable releases, keep visible
      # in nightly (prerelease) builds. .Prerelease is empty for a stable tag
      # (vX.Y.Z) and non-empty for a nightly tag (vX.Y.Z-nightly.*). Local
      # builds carry no stamp and use the package default ("true" = visible).

## Entire trail

[#1023 — Fix Scoop cli->entire upgrade path](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1023)

## Problem

#1735 renamed the Scoop package from `cli` to `entire`. Scoop resolves updates by manifest name, so existing Windows installs registered as app `cli` were orphaned when `cli.json` disappeared from the bucket: `scoop update` finds nothing and they silently stop receiving updates. The only way out for those users today is a manual uninstall + reinstall.

The CLI's own update prompt had the same blind spot: `entire`'s version-check emitted `scoop update entire/cli` for Scoop installs, which can never cross the rename to `entire/entire`.

## Fix

**Bucket side** — keep publishing `cli.json` as a **transition manifest** alongside the canonical `entire.json`:

- `depends: [entire]` — the next `scoop update cli` automatically installs the canonical `entire` package, no forced reinstall.
- `post_install` prints a migration nudge:
  `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire`
  (the `reset` recovers the shared `entire.exe` shim, which `scoop uninstall cli` can take with it — both apps ship the same shims).
- `skip_upload: auto` matching the existing entry, so prereleases don't push manifests.

GoReleaser bumps both manifests every release, so migration fires naturally on users' next update — including users who already stalled: they resume on their next `scoop update` once the next release republishes `cli.json`.

**CLI side** — fix the version-check upgrade command so an install still on the old `cli` Scoop app is steered across the rename:

- The gate is the **Scoop app dir the binary runs from** (`…\scoop\apps\cli\…` vs `…\apps\entire\…`), **not the version**. The fix only ships in a binary the user installs by updating their existing `cli` app, so by the time it runs the version is already past the rename — the app-dir name is the durable signal. Binaries on the `cli` app get the migration below; binaries already on `entire` update in place via `scoop update entire/entire`.
- The migration is **three separate one-command lines** — `scoop install entire/entire`, `scoop uninstall entire/cli`, `scoop reset entire` — install first (so a stale bucket or transient failure never removes the working CLI before its replacement is in place), then remove the old package, then `scoop reset` to re-link the shared `entire.exe` shim that uninstalling `cli` can take with it. `scoop install` auto-refreshes the bucket when >3h stale (`is_scoop_outdated` in `lib/core.ps1`; auto-update in `libexec/scoop-install.ps1`).
- **Windows is print-only — the CLI never auto-runs the update.** A running `entire.exe` holds its own shim open, so Scoop can't relink or uninstall it mid-run (install leaves the shim on the old package; uninstall fails with "still running"). So the commands are printed for the user to run once `entire` has exited — no shell operators, so each line pastes into any shell (cmd, PowerShell, git-bash). Because Windows never auto-runs, the runner stays a simple single-command exec.
- Other install managers (brew, mise, curl) are unchanged.
- README Windows section documents the same manual migration.

## Example (install still on the old `cli` Scoop app, Windows)

```text
PS C:\Users\Victor\cli> entire version
Entire CLI 0.8.0
Go version: go1.26.5
OS/Arch: windows/arm64

Update available! 0.8.0 -> 0.9.0
Release notes: https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/tag/v0.9.0
To update, run the following when entire is not running:
  scoop install entire/entire
  scoop uninstall entire/cli
  scoop reset entire
```

## Sunset

The transition entry should be dropped a few releases after migration has largely completed (noted in the config comment).

## Validation

- `goreleaser check` passes; `mise run fmt` / `mise run lint` clean.
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/` passes, incl. cases asserting the `cli`-app path emits the three-line migration, the `entire`-app path updates in place, and that Windows prints the migration (never auto-runs).
- Migration flow replayed end-to-end on a Windows VM with a local clone of the bucket:
  - resurrected the pre-rename `cli.json` from bucket history and installed it (simulated existing user),
  - committed the new `entire.json` + transition `cli.json`,
  - `scoop update cli` pulled in `entire` via `depends` and printed the migration message,
  - `scoop uninstall cli; scoop reset entire` leaves a working `entire`.

## Notes / residual risk

- Legacy users who stay on the `cli` app keep the old `apps\cli` install path that fed #1424 — the post_install nudge is the only lever to move them; verify the #1424 fix is path-independent before removing the nudge.
- Old app can't be force-removed from users' machines; the nudge is best-effort by design.
- The CLI migration command relies on Scoop's >3h staleness auto-refresh; if a user ran a scoop command <3h before migrating and the new release landed inside that window, `scoop install entire/entire` fails cleanly (missing manifest, working CLI untouched) and succeeds on retry.
